condition: suspected acute forearm compartment syndrome under a fresh plaster cast presenting with severe forearm pain on finger extension
level_rationale: Severe pain in a casted fractured right forearm triggered whenever straightening the fingers 1 day after plaster cast application is the cardinal ischemic muscle-stretch warning sign of acute forearm compartment syndrome requiring immediate emergency department cast bivalving, compartment pressure assessment, and urgent surgical evaluation to prevent permanent ischemic contracture, whereas mild itchiness of the right forearm under that cast 1 day after placement is a benign expected cast sensation appropriate for home self-care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain fracture-patient lexical register swap (-reg) + causal belief-addition clause (-att) + same-forearm benign under-cast itchiness self-care control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age 29, plaster cast placed on a broken right forearm yesterday, and severe right forearm pain on finger extension today) with a 2-word span difference (20 vs 22 words). Isolating finger-extension forearm pain in f3 avoids stranding paresthesia or tightness, and keeping 'my right forearm' and 'that cast' identical in the Rule A control ('my right forearm feels mildly itchy under that cast', supported by PMID 40456529) shifts right care cleanly from ER (level 4) to home self-care (level 1) with zero added body sites and zero stated negatives.
